sql-thinks-in-sets.author: Tunde A.
sql-thinks-in-sets.body: The GROUP BY explanation finally clicked for me. I've been writing SQL for two years and always felt like I was guessing — this framing of 'you're describing a new grouped set' changes everything.

replies.author: FTTG
replies.body: Exactly — once you see GROUP BY as a transformation into a new set rather than a sorting operation, the column restriction stops feeling arbitrary. Glad it landed.

sql-thinks-in-sets.author: Amaka O.
sql-thinks-in-sets.body: The NULL section saved me today. Had a WHERE clause that was silently dropping rows and couldn't figure out why. IS NULL vs = NULL — never making that mistake again.

sql-thinks-in-sets.author: Jide K.
sql-thinks-in-sets.body: CTEs made my queries 10x more readable. I used to nest subqueries 3 levels deep and wonder why nobody else on the team could follow what I wrote.

replies.author: Tunde A.
replies.body: Same here. The moment I started naming intermediate sets the reviews got so much faster.

thinking-in-models.author: Chisom E.
thinking-in-models.body: The habit at the end — writing a single sentence of what you expect to find before looking at the data — is deceptively simple and incredibly effective. I've started doing this every morning and my analysis work has gotten sharper.

replies.author: FTTG
replies.body: The pre-mortem energy of it is what makes it work. Forces you to commit to a hypothesis so you can't retroactively claim you knew it all along.

thinking-in-models.author: Seun B.
thinking-in-models.body: "The gap between model and reality is almost always more interesting than a number that confirms what you already believed." — this line is going on my wall.

ship-before-perfect.author: Emeka R.
ship-before-perfect.body: The distinction between correct and complete is the most useful framing I've seen on this topic. I've been using 'done' as the threshold when I should have been using 'correct'. Shipping now.

replies.author: FTTG
replies.body: That's the shift. 'Done' implies nothing left to do — 'correct' just means the core works and the learning can start.

ship-before-perfect.author: Blessing N.
ship-before-perfect.body: Setting the deadline before you start — not after — is something I wish I'd read two years ago. My last project spent three months in 'almost done' mode.

ship-before-perfect.author: Dayo F.
ship-before-perfect.body: The psychological barrier section is real. Perfectionism as risk avoidance dressed up as quality control. Hard to admit but true.

replies.author: Blessing N.
replies.body: Felt personally called out reading that part.

systems-over-goals.author: Kemi T.
systems-over-goals.body: The three properties of a good system — small enough to start, measurable but not exhausting, with a natural trigger — I've been designing systems wrong by making them too ambitious. Starting over with these as the criteria.

replies.author: FTTG
replies.body: The 'design for your worst week' framing is the key one. Most systems fail not because they're bad ideas but because they only survive the good weeks.

systems-over-goals.author: Rotimi A.
systems-over-goals.body: Goals as navigation, systems as movement. Simple distinction but it completely reframes how I think about productivity. I've been trying to get motivated to hit goals instead of just building the process.
